newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Cavallo tried to bribe magnate -lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Cavallo tried to bribe magnate -lawyer.

text.p: Argentina's former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo three years ago allegedly tried to bribe his archenemy, postal magnate Alfredo Yabran, Yabran's lawyer said in an interview published on Tuesday.
"I can tell you that Cavallo wanted to bribe Yabran three years ago, when he asked him to divide up the postal market," Yabran's lawyer Wenceslao Bunge told the La Nacion newspaper.

Cavallo, who has since left the government and relaunched himself in politics as an independent anti-corruption crusader, was in France on Tuesday. His spokesman in Argentina could not be reached for comment.

Bunge's allegations were the latest volley in a long-running verbal war between Cavallo and Yabran, whom the former minister has publicly accused of being at the center of a web of corruption stretching through Argentine business and government.
Yabran, who is suing Cavallo for libel, decided not to report the minister to the police at the time of the alleged bribe offer, Bunge said.

"Maybe we didn't report it because Cavallo at that moment was very powerful and nobody could oppose him," he said, adding that Cavallo began his public assault on Yabran after his alleged bribe offer was rejected.

The lawyer said Yabran would continue his battle in the courts against the former minister, who introduced sweeping economic reforms in Argentina before he was fired by President Carlos Menem last July.
"We are going to use all the mechanisms of judicial system...to ensure that Cavallo goes to jail," he said.

While libel is not normally punished by jail in Argentina, the sharp-tongued Cavallo has accumulated so many actions against him that he could end up behind bars if found guilty, according to political analysts and legal experts.
